reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker offers free Bitcoin in exchange for contacting him, providing a phone number, and setting up a Coinbase wallet through his link. He reinforces the offer with a projection that a small amount could become worth thousands of dollars and separately promotes his own Bitcoin mining contracts. the available video evidence does not establish whether Bitcoin was sent or whether the projected value was realized.

citations.quote: I sell bitcoin mining contracts all day long.
We have 4,000 computers up in an Iceland facility that mine Bitcoin on geothermal energy every day.
So I've got free Bitcoin coming to me every single day.
if you go to my website it's on the title of this video and you text me your phone number we're gonna have a communication or on skype gonna go ahead and send you some free bitcoin today
set up a coinbase wallet

opening.argument: The offer is presented with qualifications rather than as a guaranteed financial return. The speaker says conditions are necessary, explicitly rejects the idea that he sells Bitcoin, and describes the future-value discussion as possibility: the amount might be two or three dollars, and the increase is framed as something that may happen years later. That is consistent with a promotional giveaway accompanied by uncertainty, not a promise that viewers will receive a guaranteed profit.

citations.quote: there is some things that are necessary to go ahead and get that right there
I don't sell Bitcoin, I educate people on Bitcoin.
I may give three dollars or two dollars away guys
it may be three to five years from now

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes contact details and mining contracts, but those facts do not convert a qualified giveaway into a guaranteed-return scheme. The speaker says he is giving Bitcoin to viewers and separately discusses mining; the excerpts do not establish that viewers must buy a contract, deposit money, or accept a guaranteed outcome. Even the wallet instruction identifies a practical condition for receiving a digital transfer.

citations.quote: set up a coinbase wallet
I sell bitcoin mining contracts all day long.
send you some free bitcoin today

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the offer qualified does not resolve its central solicitation: viewers are directed to contact the speaker and provide personal contact information to receive Bitcoin. The same speaker also says he sells mining contracts. The language about possible future value may avoid an explicit guarantee, but it still supplies an enticing return narrative around the offer and does not establish that the giveaway is genuine.

you come back you're like you know what that right guy gave giving everyone that right there is worth I've got thousands and thousands of dollars

opening.argument: The video can reasonably be understood as Bitcoin education and an operational walkthrough. The speaker explicitly characterizes his role as educating people, explains how a Coinbase wallet connects to a bank account, describes confirming small bank deposits, and answers how cryptocurrency can become ordinary money. Those are instructional details about using a financial technology. The giveaway functions as a practical demonstration or incentive to help viewers set up a wallet, rather than proof that the video is selling a fraudulent investment.

citations.quote: I don't sell Bitcoin, I educate people on Bitcoin.
You hook your coin base up to your bank account.
They send two small increments to your bank.
you can swap and put money straight from your bank account into Coinbase

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats every mention of a mining business as the video's purpose, but the actual discussion is broader Bitcoin education: wallets, bank linking, exchanges, mining, and converting digital assets. Saying the speaker sells contracts does not show that this particular walkthrough requires viewers to purchase one. The offer supplies a concrete way to demonstrate the wallet process, while the excerpt does not establish a deceptive transaction or promised return.

citations.quote: How do you turn Bitcoin into real money? Very easy and great question Paul.
I sell bitcoin mining contracts all day long.
you can swap and put money straight from your bank account into Coinbase

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The educational explanations are embedded in a direct solicitation: viewers are told to contact the speaker and are promised Bitcoin. The speaker also directs viewers toward his own website and later promotes mining contracts. Explaining wallet mechanics does not show that the offer is a genuine demonstration, and the educational framing does not account for the commercial incentive surrounding the instructions.

citations.quote: go to my website, www.ResidualBitcoin.Info
I'm gonna go ahead and send you guys some free Bitcoin today
I sell bitcoin mining contracts all day long.

opening.argument: The described activity is ordinary promotion and customer contact for a cryptocurrency-related service. The speaker offers a small promotional amount, asks viewers to contact him, and explains that a Coinbase wallet is needed to receive a transfer. The material does not state that viewers must deposit money, buy a mining contract, recruit a downline, surrender passwords, or accept a guaranteed return. A referral or promotional offer should not be treated as fraudulent merely because the promoter also operates a Bitcoin business.

citations.quote: I was thinking about giving five dollars of the free Bitcoin
set up a coinbase wallet
for me to send you the money, you don't have to have that connection yet established

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a website, phone number, wallet, and mining contracts, but those are compatible with ordinary promotion and service outreach. The quoted material does not say that viewers pay the speaker or purchase a contract to qualify for the giveaway. It instead describes sending money and says the bank connection is not yet required, which weakens the claim that the observed mechanism is a deposit-based scheme.

citations.quote: you don't have to have that connection yet established
send you some free bitcoin today
I sell bitcoin mining contracts all day long.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of an explicit deposit instruction does not make the solicitation ordinary commerce. Viewers are asked for a phone number and directed to a personal website, while the speaker separately sells mining contracts. The wallet requirement and contact process create a funnel toward the speaker's cryptocurrency activity; the excerpts do not establish that the advertised Bitcoin was ever sent or that the requested contact was harmless.
